entries.subject: Gerdes et al. (2017) ALMA thermal-model diameter
entries.finding: The equal-axis size illustration uses the published thermal-model diameter of 635 km with +57/-61 km statistical and +32/-39 km systematic uncertainties, constrained by ALMA 1.3 mm thermal flux and Dark Energy Survey optical photometry; the fit assumes a spherical body with uniform surface properties and measures neither three axes nor resolved terrain.

entries.subject: cssEarth missing-coverage grid as the surface
entries.finding: No surface imagery exists for this body, so the manifest supplies the project-authored missing-coverage grid, the normal grid marks unmapped terrain and Shadows defaults off.

entries.subject: Discovery images and the ALMA detection as surface maps
entries.finding: The README records these as unresolved points rather than global textures or observed limb geometry, so they supply no surface map.
entries.revisitWhen: A resolved image, global texture or observed limb geometry of DeeDee is released.

entries.subject: Body pole, rotation period and surface attitude
entries.finding: The display uses an illustrative ICRF north pole at right ascension 0 degrees and declination +90 degrees with an arbitrary prime meridian and phase; no measured pole, rotation period or surface attitude is claimed.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured pole or rotation period for 2014 UZ224 is published.

entries.subject: Resolved companion constraints from later Hubble imaging
entries.finding: The README lists this as a useful follow-up and states that no detected satellite or later resolved shape product was verified in this source survey.
entries.revisitWhen: A published companion detection or resolved shape product changes the system interpretation.
